description:
Changes the fields sent. An empty or missing url keeps the stored one; a new one is checked like on create. Enabling a webhook clears its disabled reason and failing period; disabling it drops its waiting deliveries. A webhook restored from a backup without secrets needs its url and gets a new signing secret, shown once in the answer. Errors carry an error.<code> message id: webhook-name-taken, webhook-url-invalid, webhook-url-scheme, webhook-url-userinfo, webhook-url-required, webhook-host-unresolved, webhook-host-lookup-failed (a name lookup failed for now: try again), webhook-host-blocked (the host is, or resolves to, an address webhooks may not reach) and notify-event-not-for-webhook.

Needs: an administrator (a token needs its Administrator switch)

url.description: A new address, checked like on create. Empty or left out keeps the stored one (a webhook restored without its URL needs it). It is stored sealed and never returned

events.description: Event ids as in GET /notifications/events (an event a webhook can carry), or ["*"] for every event, also the ones added later. notification.test is never selected by "*".

enabled.description: Whether events are sent to the webhook. Default true

verify_tls.description: Whether the receiver's TLS certificate is verified (https only). Default true

200.description: The updated webhook, with secret only when a new one was made
